summary: Every course must be letter graded. You complete one set of prerequisites, which do not count toward the 45 units, and then 45 units of program coursework: the Master's Seminar and at least 34 units at the 200 level or above, with the rest at the 100 level or above. At most 9 units of research (EARTHSYS 297 and 250), 8 units of Stanford at Sea (EARTHSYS 323) and 8 units of thesis (EARTHSYS 299) count. Your advisor checks the 3.4 GPA and any course approved without a letter grade.

program.why: Grading: "All courses for the master's program must be taken for a letter grade; courses not taken for a letter grade must be approved by the master's advisor and Director of Earth Systems." An approved exception is moved in by hand.

totals.label: Research units (EARTHSYS 297, EARTHSYS 250)
totals.why: "Up to nine units of research (Earthsys 297 and/or Earthsys 250) may be completed with their Master's Advisor." One cap across both coursework rules, so research split between them is still held to 9.

totals.label: EARTHSYS 323 (Stanford at Sea)
totals.why: "Students may use 8 units of Earthsys 323: Stanford at Sea towards the required 45 units. Please note- Although the entire 16 unit course must be in your graduate career, only 8 units will be applied towards the required 45 units."

totals.label: EARTHSYS 299 (M.S. thesis)
totals.why: "Students who choose to prepare an M.S. thesis, which is not required for the degree, may take up to 8 units of EARTHSYS 299 with their master's advisor"
